company.name: Instawork
company.shortDescription: Instawork is an on-demand staffing app for gig workers and hospitality businesses.
company.description:
Instawork operates as a career marketplace for hospitality professionals. It is changing how traditional recruiting works for small businesses by turning the process into an automated matching solution. Its vision is to create economic opportunity for local businesses and professionals, globally. 

The company was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

aiResearchSummary.text: Instawork is researching and developing a Booking Engine that predicts cancellations of booked events. This system utilizes various methods and computer program products to generate predictions for distinct sequential time ranges before an event starts. This technology aims to enhance the efficiency and reliability of staffing solutions by anticipating potential disruptions in bookings. Instawork's focus is on improving the predictability and management of gig work and hospitality staffing through advanced predictive analytics.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series D round raised $60,000,000, or 40.54% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $8,095,881 to $760,000,000, a 93.87x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 65 (-13 over 90 days) and market heat at 56 (-5).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.
